newsitem.title: UK: IRA says it has dumped second Belfast mine.
newsitem.headline: IRA says it has dumped second Belfast mine.

text.p: IRA guerrillas claimed on Monday night that they had abandoned a landmine near a British military base in the Northern Ireland capital Belfast.
A caller using an Irish Republican Army identity codeword telephoned a local radio station and gave a warning that the device had been dumped near Girdwood Barracks near the residential Antrim Road.
The caller, hinting that an attack had been aborted, said the mine was abandoned because civilians were nearby.

Police said that they were investigating the claim. Security sources said they would tread warily in case of booby traps. It might be daylight before it was established if the warning was genuine, they said.

It was the second such alert in the troubled province in just over 48 hours and came on the eve of the restart of multi- party talks aimed at easing a 28 year conflict about British rule in Northern Ireland.
The IRA ended a six week period of inactivity in the province on Saturday leaving a van packed with 500 kgs of explosives in a built-up area in the west of Belfast.
In a telephone call to a radio station, an IRA representative said their "engineers" had disarmed one of their own landmines before abandoning it.
Police said a lengthy "clearance operation" had revealed that the warning was a trap, intended to lure security forces into an ambush.
Youths set fire to a van that contained the explosives stuffed into two bins. The cache did not explode.

The ending of the IRA lull and the murder of a policeman, kicked to death by pro-British Protestants on Sunday, have cast a long shadow over the resumption of the talks chaired by former U.S.senator George Mitchell.
At least 10 people have been held for police questioning about the officer's murder.
Sinn Fein is barred because the party's IRA military ally has rejected international pleas for an immediate ceasefire.
The IRA is pledged to end British control of the province and merge it in an all-Ireland state ruled from Catholic Dublin. Majority Protestants are determined to stay British.
